items.text:
I understand you!
'Thanks' is not an answer to a No-reply.  It should be: "ok, sure! I understand, thank you for your thoughts anyway.  I will ask my mom."  

The solution part is so important.  I hate being involved in the problem but not being shared the solution. It's unfair to bother someone's brain with problems,  without checking her (you)  out of the responsible circle.... 
Such things drive me crazy!

In your case I would ask, if she was able to organize someone else for her dog.
This can be perceived as caring. 
Some people might also perceive it as rude (?)
In my case I prefer to ask,  cause it releases me from the pain of not being sure who is responsible here...

Totally! 
That's the thing,  we are awesome problem solver. Burning bright!
And then we are exhausted...
Thanks! This is really helpful!
Now I am sad, wikipedia doesn't know anything about your story. There are some other stories about the origins of the tradtion...

I've also worked on being well educated / experienced to do a part-time job. Now that I have a part-time job, I realized that there are some down sides of the medal, especially if your part-time position is not well planned into the organization.

eg. I need to have the feeling of control over my tasks, but as part-time you have to give some tasks to others, without being easily able to control. You just have less control. Often I get news as the last one. I am always reacting on burning problems. There is no time to plan and think ahead. Many employers expect you to be available (on phone) if you are not in the office. You might have higher amount of communication-tasks with your team. You always have to ask / check; if the problem B is solved, if A is done, did customer B call back? You need more time to get updated, read e-mails...

Sum up: If it is a big company, and they are used to part-time employees, and they are well organized, and your job can be done with only little team-related tasks: I can recommend.

But: I don't recommend it, if it's a small company which expects same performance as full-time, has no idea what part-time means, only want to pay you less money for same work, want you to be available when you are not in the office and if responsibilities and tasks are not organized. Just don't do it. 

&#x200B;

Over all I really recommend to go to big companies with well organized structures. 

&#x200B;

wow...

Yes, the english wikipedia is telling the story, you are right.

The German wiki page is telling some different ones. But not the one with happy new year!

I'm not questioning you / your story...

I'm questioning Wikipedia itself!

that's the important part: They want to socialize with you. They don't want you to solve their problem. They just want you to "appreciate" their problem. 

Sharing problems is an accepted way of socializing. 

Actually, very often the solving of a mutual problem can lead to dissolving of the social bond.  Eg. when school is finished: no more mutual problem = people go their way = no more friendship; College = new problems = new bonds. etc. etc. 

Sometimes I have the thought, that even my boss just wants to bond with me by making up problems, that he wants me to worry about.  Another example: my sister always calls because of problems, this is making me crazy, I don't want to hear about these imaginary problems, but my therapist just got me understanding, that she just wants to connect with me.

&#x200B;
thanks I will have look!

oh girl, I'm feeling with you with every part of my body.

whatever would help I would try to arrange for you, if it's hugging or romping or crying together.

Maybe go into the woods? And scream and cry and everything? 

Is there any nature in feasible distance?

If not, just sit in your bed and cry, cry, pls let it out. Don't hurt yourself by suppressing it. Don't hurt yourself by releasing it by hurting yourself physically.

Go out and run, run, run, so you get a connection to your body again, and if you might start crying, just embrace it. 

Try to embrace the meltdown, cause this is you. This is the real connection to you.

I am sending you all my energy to be strong enough to find a place to let your feelings out. 

&#x200B;

Something I am not good at,  but what IB think would really be helpful: ask questions about the job.
The goal should be, that you get to know the job better. 
How is the atmosphere, How they handle issues. Why the job is vacant. With whom you are working directly with...
Do not ask exactly this questions. But ask questions that lead them to answers that are disclosing that information. 
Eg. Can you tell me a situation where an employee didn't do a good job?  pls describe how you handled the situation. 
--> by this you will learn how they cope with mistakes.
You remind me that I was being bullied by being called 'slow' for all my teenage years.
same for my parents.

sry, sometimes I'm the one staring, but I don't know why, but I would immediately look away if you'd look back at me!

&#x200B;
I experience that I cannot listen to what somebody is saying when I have to look in the eyes. It's like a senseless task that I have to do.
this is an important point!
yes, she looks like she's jugding me or making fun of me or is angry on me...
love your comment and approach to things

sure. I have an apointment on friday with a neurologist. I have the date since 2 months. Since a few days it's becoming real and I am so afraid of it. I also started a folder and lists to gather all hints, references, memories, feelings and other thoughts.

I am mostly afraid to start masking / playing a role during the diagnosis. Sometimes I think a robot as examiner would be helpful, so that I don't have to react on a social level. Which would distract me from the facts. 

My journey led me from depressions to social phobia to aspergers. My GP and my therapist convinced me to let me check. In the country where I live only a neurologist is allowed to give a first diagnosis and to send me to a special outpatient clinic for ASD. So there are barriers but only bureaucratical not financial.

My recent fear is that I'm not aware of possible disadvantages of getting a diagnosis....

I do the same!  I love to 'brush' my arms with my fingernails. It gives me such a release, a pleasant feeling.
Yes it focuses my brain new... 

Always such an experience to browse through our subreddit.

items.title: DAE experience the feeling of cold blood in their body when being ill?
items.text:
DAE experience the feeling of cold blood in their body when being ill?
[removed]

I either read fiction or non-fiction. 

For my first 10-15 years of reading I only read ficiton, and I did it excessively.

From one day to another I stopped.  Ever since I prefer non-fiction.

Sometimes I think I sucked enough knowledge about storys out of fiction to be able to concentrate on non-fiction...?

You are me.

I'm 31, also self diagnosed since January and having an appointment tomorrow with a neurologist. 

I took some notes, but nothing more...

I am torn. As a teenager I loved these young adult fantasy girl books. I was obsessed with them, read them multiple times... Since around my 25th birthday I don't read fiction anymore. 

And I never read such a book for adult women...

Actually I think I only read what gives me benefit in my real life. As a teenager I had to learn and copy these social stories from books. It was my SI. Now I am more interested into social philosophy, so I read papers and books about this "on a higher level".

Hi there, I saw your post on the face blindness. I'm sorry.  This is such a bummer.
I only got a prescription to a specialist. And the prescription now says "strong suspicion of ASD" before it said "suspicion of ASD".  
Nevertheless I was released and decided to tell two friends of mine that I'm seeking a diagnosis of ASD. This was the super weird part of the day.  I feel horrible ever since. They didn't do something wrong. They were just struggling, they were not prepared. They don't know what it means. I just have the feeling now that it was a mistake to tell them...

In a positive or negative way? 
Only curious...

Yeah, techno and electronic music. Dub step! 
Techno Festivals are also the only ones I can enjoy.

Awesome idea! 

But please don't only show one aspie in a group of  NT / hetero / cis - people.
Show a different  girls / older women / children / boys on the spectrum. And let them interact with cis/ lgbtq/ physically disabled people. 
It would be awesome to show variety.

Ah,... Just let your creativity flow,  don't listen to me ;)

I have the same feet and last year I discovered that there are techniques how to lace shoes so they are firm at the ankles but loose at the front.  I will look for a link  for you... 
And yes, hypermobilty here  as well.
